short: Joint LSTM decoding on mouth pixels (M06) is ahead of 2015 lipreading, but pixel-input networks date to 1994 and the 8.3-point gain is over linear SVMs, not HMMs.
position: The paper changes decoding (M06): a feed-forward layer and two LSTM layers trained jointly on mouth crops replace hand-crafted features and a separate classifier [@wand2016lipreading]. The design is ahead of its field: of 159 lip-reading studies first public before 2015-07, 113 name an HMM and 2 a recurrent network, and no read prior trains a recurrent model together with its visual front end (Appendix); the gain repeats on two disjoint speaker groups. Learning from raw lip pixels is not new, since an uncited 1994 time-delay network was trained on gray-level lip pixels [@duchnowski1994see]; what is new is recurrent memory over the word. Pre-cut word clips (M04) and per-speaker splits (M12) are standard for the time and stated by the authors. The only baselines are linear SVMs on a six-frame vector, with no HMM although 113 of 159 prior studies name one (Appendix), so the gain is over a non-sequential classifier, not the usual pipeline. The 11.6% gain is relative, 8.3 points absolute (inference), and the t-test has no stated sample unit.
